references.text: The regulation concerning the goat as a sin offering for leaders in Israel, showing the background of this offering at the consecration of the tabernacle.
A goat is used as a sin offering, the same type of offering that tribal leaders brought at the consecration of the tabernacle.
The goat as a sin offering on the Day of Atonement, highlighting the central role this animal played in atonement rituals.
Goat as a sin offering for the entire congregation, the same type of offering used at the consecration.
Goat as a sin offering at the New Moon festival, showing the continuation of this sacrificial practice in Israel's worship.
Goats as sin offerings during Hezekiah's temple cleansing, illustrating the use of this sacrifice at major sanctuary dedications.
Goats as sin offerings at the consecration of the rebuilt temple, reflecting the offering made at the tabernacle's consecration.
